biography: Gabriel Miranda, a Sao Paulo native, carries the spirit of Brazilian motorsport in his blood. Growing up near Interlagos, the roar of engines was his lullaby. His father, a mechanic for a local touring car team, instilled in him a deep appreciation for the mechanics and strategy of racing. Gabriel's entry into the sport was almost accidental. Filling in for a sick driver in a Copa Fusca race at Interlagos, he stunned everyone by qualifying mid-pack and finishing a respectable seventh. This impromptu performance ignited a passion, and he's been chasing the checkered flag ever since. Now partnered with F.Goncalves Skin in the #888 Copa Fusca entry, Gabriel is considered to be at the peak of his abilities, though his inconsistent temperament sometimes gets in the way of achieving consistent results.
drivingStyle: Miranda's driving style is a blend of raw aggression and calculated risk. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the limits in corners, often flirting with disaster. While this approach can yield spectacular results, it also leads to inconsistencies. He's a master of tire management when focused, but pressure can sometimes cause him to overdrive, leading to costly mistakes. His ability to adapt to changing track conditions is a strong suit, allowing him to capitalize on opportunities that others might miss.
rivalries: Ricardo Vargas: A long-standing rivalry stemming from a controversial collision that cost Vargas a championship in Gabriel's rookie year.
Isabela Oliveira: A fierce on-track battle for position frequently results in close calls and heated exchanges after the race.
Joao Silva: A rivalry fueled by a clash of personalities and differing approaches to racing etiquette.
quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, regardless of the weather.
Before each race, he listens to a specific samba song to calm his nerves.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about heart. If you're not willing to risk it all, you're not truly racing."
careerHighlight: Winning the Copa Fusca championship in 2021 after a season-long battle, securing the title in the final race with a daring last-lap overtake.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the 2022 Interlagos 500 after a mechanical failure, costing him a home-soil victory and damaging his team's morale.
